mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs and increased equity discounting.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the previous 12 months' returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by rising consumer confidence (HOUST) predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as labor market strength supports corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 3 months average AND HOUST > previous 3 months average
failure_condition: In 20 out of 30 such triggered windows, the 60-day forward return is negative or flat (cumulative return < baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests weakening supply-side constraints, which tends to coincide with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as demand absorption improves.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND INDPRO < (previous month * 0.98)
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly drop in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 0.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as the market anticipates a disinflationary trend that may pressure growth stocks.
failure_condition: In 8 such events, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for the first time in three months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is more likely to be positive due to expectations of continued economic expansion and reduced policy tightening.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4 AND UNRATE < previous month AND UNRATE < month_before_previous
failure_condition: Across 15 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of cases (proportion > 0.6).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in payrolls (PAYEMS) above 150,000 jobs followed by a sustained rise in consumer spending proxies (HOUST) predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as momentum in labor and consumer markets supports earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 150000 AND HOUST > previous 2 months average
failure_condition: In 12 such events, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (GDPC1) of over 10% in any quarter is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as market participants anticipate softening demand and profit compression.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous quarter AND GDPC1 < (previous quarter * 0.9)
failure_condition: Across 5 such quarters, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be negative due to expectations of tighter credit conditions and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: In 10 such windows, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
